decls.description: The thirteen relations of Allen between two intervals with both bounds stated. Exactly one holds for any two such intervals; the rule allen derives it for two different intervals of one series.

contains.description: b starts after a starts and ends before a ends

during.description: a starts after b starts and ends before b ends

equals.description: a and b start together and end together

finished_by.description: b starts after a starts, and they end together

finishes.description: a starts after b starts, and they end together

overlapped_by.description: b starts first, a starts inside b, and b ends inside a

overlaps.description: a starts first, b starts inside a, and a ends inside b

started_by.description: a and b start together, and b ends first

starts.description: a and b start together, and a ends first

decls.description: How an interval stands at a reference. Exactly one holds for an interval and a reference on the same axis. A domain binds it to a tone and gives its own words. positive, no_end and attention with the reason end_within_horizon stand only where the interval holds at the reference.

attention.description: the interval holds and its end lies within the horizon, or the end has come and the extension has not

negative.description: the end has come, and the extension too where one is stated

no_end.description: the interval holds, and is stated to have no end

not_begun.description: a stated start lies ahead of the reference, and the end has not come

positive.description: the interval holds, and its end lies further ahead than the horizon of the reference

unknown.description: nobody recorded the end, or the start, nor that there is none, so whether the interval holds is unknown

decls.description: Why an interval has its judgement. One reason per judgement; it tells apart two rows of one value. A domain gives its own words per reason.

end_beyond_horizon.description: the end lies further ahead than the horizon

end_not_recorded.description: nobody recorded an end, nor that there is none

end_within_horizon.description: the end lies ahead, within the horizon

ended.description: the end has come, and no extension is stated

extension_ended.description: the end has come, and the extension has stopped

in_extension.description: the end has come, and the extension runs

start_ahead.description: a stated start lies ahead of the reference: the interval has not begun

start_not_recorded.description: the end lies ahead, and nobody recorded a start, nor that there is none

without_end.description: the interval holds, and is stated to have no end

decls.description: A side of an interval that can be stated to have no bound.

start.description: the interval has no first position: it has always been

decls.description: Anything a domain reads as lasting from a position up to, and not including, a later one. A view supplies its elements.

slots.description: The axis its positions are counted on. Positions on different axes are never compared.
The first position it covers. Open world: an interval without this row and without unbounded start has a start nobody recorded, which is unknown.
The first position it no longer covers. Open world: an interval without this row and without unbounded end has an end nobody recorded, which is unknown.

The sides on which it is stated to have no bound: a claim with an origin of its own, such as a decision without a term or a contract for an indefinite time. Never the default: a record that is silent about a bound states nothing.
The first position an extension beyond the end no longer covers. Between end and extension_end the interval is in its extension.

The position from which the interval is known (knowledge time, apart from what it covers). Open world (W6): an interval without this row has a knowledge time nobody recorded, which is unknown, never "known from the first position on".
The series it is read in, together with the other intervals of that series. The rule allen relates two intervals of one series only.

decls.description: A named axis of whole-number positions with one unit and one zero: a calendar counted in days, or the order of a set of stages. In a proof it is the join between an interval and a reference, not a reason, so its steps are folded.
Intervals that are read together: the successive states of one thing, or the divisions of one whole. All intervals of a series lie on one axis.
A position for which the intervals are read: what holds at it, and how each interval stands at it. A fact, never the clock, and itself a choice of the reader.

slots.description: The axis its position is counted on.
How far ahead of the position an end counts as near, in positions of the axis. Zero when nothing counts as near.

lines: // Rules of std-time, in the Datalog subset, so Soufflé is the oracle.
// The base relations are the theory's tables: interval__on_axis(i, l), interval__start(i, s),
// interval__end(i, e), interval__unbounded(i, side), interval__extension_end(i, x), interval__known_from(i, k),
// interval__in_series(i, q), reference_point__on_axis(r, l), reference_point__position(r, p) and
// reference_point__horizon(r, h).
// A position is a whole number on an axis. An interval is half-open: it covers start <= p < end. Positions are
// compared only on one axis.
// A bound has three states. It is stated: a row in start or end. It is stated to be absent: a row in
// unbounded ("start" or "end"), a claim with an origin of its own. Or nobody recorded it: neither row, and
// then it is unknown. start and end are open, so a rule says something about a bound only from a row
// that is there; no rule reads a missing row as "it has no bound", and no rule puts a number in its place.
.decl start_stated(interval: symbol)
start_stated(i) :- interval__start(i, s).
.decl end_stated(interval: symbol)
end_stated(i) :- interval__end(i, e).
.decl extension_stated(interval: symbol)
extension_stated(i) :- interval__extension_end(i, x).
.decl known_from_stated(interval: symbol)
known_from_stated(i) :- interval__known_from(i, k).
// Nobody recorded a start for interval i, nor that it has none. About the registration, not the world: the
// interval started somewhere or never did, and the record does not say which.
// @absence
.decl start_not_recorded(interval: symbol)
start_not_recorded(i) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), !start_stated(i), !interval__unbounded(i, "start").
// Nobody recorded an end for interval i, nor that it has none.
// @absence
.decl end_not_recorded(interval: symbol)
end_not_recorded(i) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), !end_stated(i), !interval__unbounded(i, "end").
// Nobody recorded from which position interval i is known. Whether it was known at a reference is
// then unknown: known_at has no row for it.
// @absence
.decl known_from_not_recorded(interval: symbol)
known_from_not_recorded(i) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), !known_from_stated(i).
// Axiom: an interval is proper. Where both bounds are stated, the start lies before the end.
// @invariant
.decl interval_inverted(interval: symbol)
interval_inverted(i) :- interval__start(i, s), interval__end(i, e), e <= s.
// Axiom: a bound is not both stated and stated to be absent.
// @invariant
.decl bound_contradicted(interval: symbol)
bound_contradicted(i) :- interval__start(i, s), interval__unbounded(i, "start").
bound_contradicted(i) :- interval__end(i, e), interval__unbounded(i, "end").
// Axiom: an extension does not stop before the end it extends.
// @invariant
.decl extension_inverted(interval: symbol)
extension_inverted(i) :- interval__end(i, e), interval__extension_end(i, x), x < e.
// Axiom: an extension extends a stated end. Where no end is recorded, or the interval is stated to have
// none, there is nothing to extend.
// @invariant
.decl extension_without_end(interval: symbol)
extension_without_end(i) :- interval__extension_end(i, x), end_not_recorded(i).
extension_without_end(i) :- interval__extension_end(i, x), interval__unbounded(i, "end").
// Axiom: the intervals of one series lie on one axis, so their positions can be compared.
// @invariant
.decl series_across_axes(series: symbol)
series_across_axes(q) :- interval__in_series(a, q), interval__in_series(b, q), interval__on_axis(a, l),
interval__on_axis(b, m), l != m.
// begun_at: at reference r the first position of interval i has come, or i is stated to have no start. An
// interval whose start nobody recorded has no row: whether it has begun is unknown.
.decl begun_at(interval: symbol, at: symbol)
begun_at(i, r) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__start(i, s), s <= p.
begun_at(i, r) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__unbounded(i, "start").
// ended_at: at reference r the end of interval i has come. The end is the first position i no longer covers.
// An interval whose end nobody recorded has no row.
.decl ended_at(interval: symbol, at: symbol)
ended_at(i, r) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__end(i, e), e <= p.
// holds_at: interval i covers the position of reference r. It has begun, and its end is known to lie ahead:
// a stated end after the position, or a statement that it has none. Never from the absence of an end.
.decl holds_at(interval: symbol, at: symbol)
holds_at(i, r) :- begun_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p), interval__end(i, e), p < e.
holds_at(i, r) :- begun_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p), interval__unbounded(i, "end").
// in_extension: the end of i has come at r, and the end of its extension has not.
.decl in_extension(interval: symbol, at: symbol)
in_extension(i, r) :- ended_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p), interval__extension_end(i, x), p < x.
// known_at: at reference r interval i is known: its stated known_from has come. An interval whose
// known_from nobody recorded has no row: known_from_not_recorded names it. Knowledge is apart from
// what the interval covers: a domain reads holds_at at one reference and known_at at another.
.decl known_at(interval: symbol, at: symbol)
known_at(i, r) :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__known_from(i, k), k <= p.
// judgement: how interval i stands at reference r, and why. Exactly one row per interval and
// reference on one axis, decided in this order:
//   1. the end has come: negative (ended, extension_ended) or attention (in_extension), whatever the start;
//   2. else a stated start lies ahead: not_begun (start_ahead), whatever the end;
//   3. else nobody recorded the end: unknown (end_not_recorded);
//   4. else nobody recorded the start: unknown (start_not_recorded);
//   5. else the interval holds, and its end decides: no_end, attention (end_within_horizon) or positive.
// A tone that reassures (positive, attention within the horizon, no_end) stands exactly where holds_at has
// a row. "Not ended" and "not begun" are never read from a missing row: each clause names the bound it
// rests on, stated, stated to be absent, or not recorded (start and end are open, W6).
.decl judgement(interval: symbol, at: symbol, value: symbol, reason: symbol)
judgement(i, r, "negative", "ended") :- ended_at(i, r), interval__end(i, e), !extension_stated(i).
judgement(i, r, "negative", "extension_ended") :- ended_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__extension_end(i, x), x <= p.
judgement(i, r, "attention", "in_extension") :- in_extension(i, r), interval__extension_end(i, x).
judgement(i, r, "not_begun", "start_ahead") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
reference_point__position(r, p), interval__start(i, s), p < s, interval__end(i, e), p < e.
judgement(i, r, "not_begun", "start_ahead") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
reference_point__position(r, p), interval__start(i, s), p < s, interval__unbounded(i, "end").
judgement(i, r, "not_begun", "start_ahead") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
reference_point__position(r, p), interval__start(i, s), p < s, end_not_recorded(i).
judgement(i, r, "unknown", "end_not_recorded") :- begun_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p),
end_not_recorded(i).
judgement(i, r, "unknown", "end_not_recorded") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
start_not_recorded(i), end_not_recorded(i).
judgement(i, r, "unknown", "start_not_recorded") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
reference_point__position(r, p), start_not_recorded(i), interval__end(i, e), p < e.
judgement(i, r, "unknown", "start_not_recorded") :- interval__on_axis(i, l), reference_point__on_axis(r, l),
start_not_recorded(i), interval__unbounded(i, "end").
judgement(i, r, "no_end", "without_end") :- holds_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p),
interval__unbounded(i, "end").
judgement(i, r, "attention", "end_within_horizon") :- holds_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p),
reference_point__horizon(r, h), interval__end(i, e), p < e, t = p + h, e <= t.
judgement(i, r, "positive", "end_beyond_horizon") :- holds_at(i, r), reference_point__position(r, p),
reference_point__horizon(r, h), interval__end(i, e), t = p + h, t < e.
// span: an interval of a series with both bounds stated, and proper.
.decl span(interval: symbol, series: symbol, start: number, end: number)
span(i, q, s, e) :- interval__in_series(i, q), interval__start(i, s), interval__end(i, e), s < e.
// allen: the relation of Allen between two different intervals of one series, both with a span. Exactly one
// of the thirteen holds for each ordered pair. The number of rows grows with the square of a series.
// @explain on_demand
.decl allen(a: symbol, b: symbol, relation: symbol)
allen(a, b, "before") :- span(a, q, _, e), span(b, q, t, _), e < t.
allen(a, b, "meets") :- span(a, q, _, e), span(b, q, e, _).
allen(a, b, "overlaps") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, f), s < t, t < e, e < f.
allen(a, b, "starts") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, s, f), e < f.
allen(a, b, "during") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, f), t < s, e < f.
allen(a, b, "finishes") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, e), t < s.
allen(a, b, "equals") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, s, e), a != b.
allen(a, b, "after") :- span(a, q, s, _), span(b, q, _, f), f < s.
allen(a, b, "met_by") :- span(a, q, s, _), span(b, q, _, s).
allen(a, b, "overlapped_by") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, f), t < s, s < f, f < e.
allen(a, b, "started_by") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, s, f), f < e.
allen(a, b, "contains") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, f), s < t, f < e.
allen(a, b, "finished_by") :- span(a, q, s, e), span(b, q, t, e), s < t.
.output start_stated, end_stated, extension_stated, known_from_stated, start_not_recorded, end_not_recorded
.output known_from_not_recorded
.output interval_inverted, bound_contradicted, extension_inverted, extension_without_end, series_across_axes
.output begun_at, ended_at, holds_at, in_extension, known_at, judgement, span, allen

module.description: Intervals of positions on an axis. A position is a whole number on a named axis: a day counted on a calendar, or the rank of a stage. An interval is half-open: it covers start <= p < end. A bound is stated, or stated to be absent, or not recorded; a bound nobody recorded is unknown, never a number and never "no bound", and so is a knowledge time nobody recorded. A reference is a position for which the intervals are read: a fact, never the clock. The axioms and the derived relations are in rules/time.dl. The mapping annotations compare with OWL-Time; no rule reads them.
